name: AlgoTune
description: AlgoTune is a benchmark of 154–155 widely used math, physics, and computer-science functions, paired with a framework for validating and timing LM-synthesized solution code against reference implementations from popular open-source packages (SciPy, scikit-learn, CVXPY, etc.). For each function, the model must produce code that is faster than the reference while matching its outputs on a held-out test set. The accompanying AlgoTuner agent achieves an average 1.72× speedup over reference solvers, and analyses show current models predominantly perform library-level substitutions and code refactoring rather than discovering new algorithmic constructs.
evaluation_method: speedup ratio between candidate and reference solver on held-out inputs, gated on output equivalence
general_score_metric: geometric mean speedup over reference implementations (held-out inputs)
typical_sota_score: AlgoTuner agent ~1.72× average speedup; surface-level optimizations dominate over genuine algorithmic discovery
reputation: NeurIPS 2025 paper; cited by Epoch AI as a key non-saturating optimization benchmark where humans set a baseline but the metric continues past parity.
notes: 154 coding tasks collected from domain experts plus a validation/timing harness. Reference implementations are drawn from popular open-source numerical packages. Designed to stay informative even after human-baseline parity, since the speedup metric has no natural ceiling. Failure analysis indicates current LMs rarely produce true algorithmic innovations.
